comments.text:
I'm not sure about this. But since I'm here, and the topic is interesting enough, I'll try this.

In terms of gaming.

With 10x faster reactions via 10x brain speed, everything seems slow. But I think being a puzzle gamer would be addictive... You would think 10 times faster, but not 10 times "better", so a very difficult puzzle will still feel soul crushing until you solve it, and still be satisfying to you when you do solve it. It does have to be so hard that there are no brute force routes, you have to actually reason through the puzzle. The threshold for "can't brute force" might need to be higher though, or maybe just self-imposed.

But once you are developing your ability to think better, not just faster. You'll complete ten times as many puzzles as your normal-speed peers, where as normally, an extremely hard puzzle is a massive time sink.

Sure, there's being the world's greatest speedrunner. But when a game feels 10x as long, it seems mentally taxing like playing a rhythm game that's too slow. You would rather play a real rhythm game, modded to be 10x as fast.

Then outside of gaming... Basically any mind-oriented job that you can grasp. Even being an artist would work.

comments.text:
some fun rough calculations i did 
(how far away bullet would need to be fired to dodge it)

if we estimate a moving bullet to be moving at ~500 mph (223.52 meters per second)
223.52*0.025= ~5.6m
you will realize a bullet is moving towards you before it hits you at 5.6m.

assuming u have speed roughly equal to codemtc 
(recent video of him cutting a pumpkin EXTREMELY estimated total distance traveled 1m in time 0.56s meaning he can move at roughly 1.8 m/s)
and moving a body out of the way would be 1/2 av. width of a shoulder span (~0.4m)
you would need 0.72s to move.
distance for bullet to travel while dodging: 223.52*0.72= ~160.9m

a bullet would need to be fired 166.5m away for you to react and dodge in time reliably
for freedom units, its 546.2 feet away or 1.5 american football pitches away

obviously if a bullet is 1000 mph then it would be double the distance

BUT 0.72s to move seems like too long so im doing another distance calculation for 0.5s cause u can rotate ur body sideways so its quicker to dodge
this would make it so the bullet would need to be fired ~111.8 meters away to move and 117.4m to react and dodge. again, for you burger eating westerns its 385 feet or 1.07 football pitches

thank you for listening to my ted talk
Edit: if im wrong on anything, please correct me
